message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "---
name: test

concurrency:
    group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
    cancel-in-progress: true

on:
    push:
        branches: [master]
    pull_request:
        branches: ['*']

jobs:

    unit_test:

        strategy:
            fail-fast: false
            matrix:
                python-version: ['3.10', '3.11', '3.12', '3.13', '3.14']

        runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        steps:
        -   uses: actions/checkout@v6
            with:
                fetch-depth: 0

        -   name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
            uses: actions/setup-python@v6
            with:
                python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
                allow-prereleases: true

        -   name: Cache pip dependencies
            uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
                path: ~/.cache/pip
                key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
                restore-keys: |
                    ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

        -   name: Install dependencies
            run: |
                sudo apt-get update
                python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools

        -   name: Install
            run: python -m pip install .[test]

        -   name: Test
            run: python -m pytest --pyargs atlasreader --cov=atlasreader

        -   name: Coveralls
            uses: coverallsapp/github-action@v2

        -   name: Test notebooks
            run: |
                pip install nbval
                for n in `ls notebooks/*ipynb`
                do
                    pytest --nbval-lax -v -s ${n};
                done
",
  "rationale": "The workflow installs Python dependencies on every run across five Python versions with no dependency cache, so repeated PyPI fetching occurs. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern is supported (reviewed, reported_benefit; modest VM-time reduction) and its preconditions are met: pyproject.toml exists as a stable cache input, no equivalent cache already exists, and the cached content is ordinary PyPI wheels rather than mutable/untrusted build outputs. Adding an actions/cache step for ~/.cache/pip keyed on hashFiles('pyproject.toml') before dependency installation preserves every existing build and test step (checkout, setup, install, pytest with coverage, Coveralls, notebook tests) and changes nothing about permissions, triggers, or required checks.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
